QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_74

question.text: Jeevan Jyoti Foundation runs a combined Healthcare + Slum-Development programme (mobile clinics INSIDE a slum-rehabilitation zone). This spans SAS-200 and SAS-1100. The SIA's integrated approach should:

answer.text: Prepare a single Social Impact Assessment Report with TWO standard-specific indicator sets, clearly delineated; shared infrastructure (e.g., drinking-water construction) reported once under the primary standard with cross-reference to the secondary
Use SAS-200 only since health is the primary activity
Prepare two completely independent reports with no cross-linkage

explanation.text: The Logic: For a programme spanning multiple SAS thematic areas (here SAS-200 and SAS-1100), the cleanest design is a single integrated Social Impact Assessment Report containing two standard-specific indicator sets that are clearly delineated, with shared infrastructure reported once under the primary standard and cross-referenced to the secondary. This balances transparency with avoidance of double-counting. The Trap: Using SAS-200 only ignores the housing/slum-rehabilitation dimension. Two completely independent reports with no cross-linkage create reconciliation problems. Letting the donor choose abandons the SIA's independent professional judgement. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) says the relevant SAS thematic area should be chosen by activity and notes multi-dimensional projects may have sector convergence, but does not prescribe a single integrated report with two indicator sets and a primary-standard cross-reference treatment for shared infrastructure on the pages reviewed. The framing above reflects general integrated-reporting practice.
